title: House burglary during amphetamine-fueled paranoia
kyle_arnold_account: Incident occurs during 'zenith of Dick's amphetamine-fueled paranoia'; windows smashed, reinforced file cabinet broken open, asbestos scattered. Arnold argues Dick fabricated this event (Chapter 6) as a coverup: the burglary was actually self-inflicted by Dick himself.
sutin_account: Burglary remains 'a much-discussed unsolved riddle of Dick's life.' Dick's imagination ran wild speculating about CIA operatives, Black Panthers, or political thugs. Later became legendary through Rolling Stone article.
religious_context: Not directly religious, but sets pattern of paranoid theorizing that would intensify toward 2-3-74.
people_involved: Philip K. Dick, police, various suspected burglar categories
significance: Paradigmatic instance of Dick's inability to distinguish reality from imagination; pattern of paranoid ideation and creative theorizing that would resurface in 2-3-74.

title: Dark-haired delivery girl with golden fish sign necklace
kyle_arnold_account: Arnold notes the 'dark-haired delivery girl' incident was the triggering event. Dick was impacted wisdom tooth extraction, received sodium pentothal during surgery, prescribed Darvon pain medication. The delivery of medication coincided with Dick's encounter with the young woman wearing the Christian fish sign necklace. Arnold emphasizes the mundane medical context.
sutin_account: The delivery girl 'stood staring at her, amazed, also confused, thinking I'd never seen such a beautiful girl' (Dick's account). She wore 'a fascinating gold necklace' with a fish. When asked about it, she replied 'This is a sign used by the early Christians.' The girl then departed. Sutin notes Dick felt 'certain for the first time that he was—not as an individual, but as a spiritual entity—immortal.'
religious_context: The Christian fish sign (ichthys) functioned as the primary trigger for Dick's entire 2-3-74 sequence. The girl represented the anima archetype (Jungian)—embodying the 'dark-haired girl' obsession from Dick's entire life. Dick placed himself in role of 'secret Christian,' which necessitated hiding from persecutors (ancient Rome).
location: Dick's apartment, California (Fullerton area where he lived with Tessa)
people_involved: Philip K. Dick, unnamed dark-haired delivery girl (pharmacy delivery), Tessa B. Dick (wife)
significance: Initiating event of 2-3-74. According to Sutin's first comprehensive Exegesis study, this moment triggered visions of past lives, genetic memories, and awakening to 'celestial origins.' Arnold disputes the mystical interpretation, emphasizing the pharmaceutical and psychological vulnerability (post-surgery, pain medication).

title: Visions of ancient Rome superimposed over modern environment
kyle_arnold_account: Arnold frames these as hallucinatory experiences accompanying the fish-sign trigger and medication effects. The paranoid structure (Rome as oppressor, Christians as persecuted) reflects Dick's pre-existing paranoid ideation extending back years.
sutin_account: 'In March I looked around and saw Rome! Rome everywhere! Power and force, stone walls, iron bars.' Dick 'pierced the veil' and saw ancient Roman Empire dominating the landscape. This vision structured around the fish sign: 'By flashing Dick the fish sign, the dark-haired delivery girl placed him in the role of a secret Christian. As such, Dick had to be hiding from somebody, and that somebody, for ancient Christians, had been ancient Rome.'
religious_context: Core mystical framework: Time frozen at 50 A.D. by Roman Empire machinations; modern world is illusion concealing ancient reality. Christians (including Dick) are persecuted insurgents. This becomes foundational cosmology for Exegesis and VALIS.
location: Fullerton, California neighborhood; Dick's apartment and surrounding areas
people_involved: Philip K. Dick, Tessa B. Dick
significance: First major visual component of 2-3-74. Establishes the Black Iron Prison metaphor central to all subsequent Dick theology. Visions were 'primarily rooted in...justice, truth, and freedom' and drove Dick to write letters to Congress about Nixon.

title: Infant son Christopher baptism with hot dog bun and chocolate Ovaltine
kyle_arnold_account: Arnold documents this as instance of Dick's religious preoccupation overwhelming rational judgment. Dick 'became terrified that his family was in danger of supernatural attack.' Used available food items rather than proper sacramental materials, reflecting both urgency and bizarreness.
sutin_account: Tessa describes: 'Phil put the hot dog aside because meat wouldn't be appropriate for a baptism, dipped his finger into the Ovaltine and drew a cross on Chris's forehead with it, and then he gave him a bite of the hot dog bun and a drink of the Ovaltine.' Dick elaborated this in VALIS.
religious_context: Demonstrates Dick's idiosyncratic religious invention—using Christian ritual form but with personalized content. Reflects belief that infant required protection from supernatural forces. Shows merger of mundane reality (child's favorite food) with sacred significance.
people_involved: Philip K. Dick, Christopher (infant son), Tessa B. Dick
significance: Example of how 2-3-74 manifested in daily behavior. Arnold notes it shows Dick functioning with concern for others (son's protection) despite mental disturbance. Paradoxical combination of 'gravity and goofiness.'

title: Vision: 'The Restorer of What Was Lost, The Mender of What Was Broken'
kyle_arnold_account: Arnold interprets as part of dissociative re-integration fantasy. Dick felt his personality was 'broken into pieces'; 2-3-74 provided experience of intense wholeness that temporarily 'mended these breaks.' Temporary amelioration of longstanding dissociative symptoms.
sutin_account: Dick writes to Claudia Bush March 21, 1975 (one year later): 'I speak of The Restorer of What Was Lost The Mender of What Was Broken.' Described as 'vivid fire, with shining colors' appearing on March 16. Core theme: integration of spirit and body after lifetime of dissociative alienation.
religious_context: Divine presence takes up residence inside Dick. Experience of wholeness contrasts with lifelong fragmentation. Represents temporary healing through mystical contact.
people_involved: Philip K. Dick, the mystical 'It' (divine presence)
significance: Peak moment of 2-3-74's positive integrative function. Demonstrates how experience felt genuinely healing, not purely pathological. Arnold acknowledges Dick 'made better decisions and took better care of himself than usual' during this period.

title: Divine presence declares 'the world did not compute'
kyle_arnold_account: Arnold notes the predominant visual and cerebral quality of Dick's experience; 'a fire in the mind, not the heart or gut.' Shows Dick's particular phenomenology: intellectual understanding rather than emotional or somatic experience.
sutin_account: 'It, from inside me, looked out and saw that the world did not compute, that I—and it—had been lied to. It denied the reality, and power, and authenticity, of the world.' The words 'looked' and 'saw' indicate predominantly visual quality. The phrase 'did not compute' has cerebral tone.
religious_context: Core gnosis: material world is false; reality hidden beneath. Parallels Gnostic cosmology where false demiurge rules material plane while true God/Pleroma waits beyond the veil.
people_involved: Philip K. Dick, the divine presence ('It')
significance: Peak philosophical revelation moment. Establishes epistemological challenge that haunts Exegesis: How to distinguish true revelation from delusion?

title: Sustained visionary period: 'Tireless' passion and sense of purity and justice
kyle_arnold_account: Arnold notes Dick 'often had long periods of being bedridden, unable to work or even attend to daily tasks.' 2-3-74 lent Dick unprecedented 'font of tireless passion that felt inexhaustible. It was better than amphetamines.' Shows marked improvement in functioning.
sutin_account: From March 20 Dick writes of unceasing revelations revealing contamination of world with falsehood and injustice. 'The historical process of contamination by which that falsehood had come to hide the truth was also unveiled.' Dick felt fighting for 'pure justice and truth.'
religious_context: Experience of divine guidance and purpose. Dick believed he was instrumental in Nixon's impeachment through letters to Congress. Wrote 'letter after letter to Congress identifying the deceptions in Nixon's transcripts.'
people_involved: Philip K. Dick, Tessa B. Dick, Congress members, Richard Nixon administration
significance: Longest sustained peak of 2-3-74. Shows paradox: Dick's outward behavior more effective than usual (financial improvement, better self-care) while inner world extremely turbulent. Arnold: 'his outward behavior was more effective than usual, not less.'

title: Golden Rectangle vision: doorway to spiritual paradise
kyle_arnold_account: Arnold catalogs this as part of Dick's visionary landscape. Dick experienced rectangle as abstract figure, then embodied in environment. Vision of 'pylon or arch-like doorway' opening onto peaceful world.
sutin_account: Dick perceived 'a lovely quiet peaceful world on the other side, waiting.' He heard 'bells and the lady singing...and the golden rectangle doorway with the sea and figure beyond, and the moonlight.' Dick felt vision 'explained everything' though explanation could not be articulated. 'Dick got a glimpse of paradise.'
religious_context: Positive visionary access point to divine realm. Contrasts with darker paranoid visions of persecution. Rectangle made of pink light in one instance—connection to the 'pink light' of VALIS.
location: Dick's bedroom and surrounding home environment
significance: Benign counterpart to persecutional visions. Shows range of 2-3-74 experiences—from combative/paranoid to peaceful/integrative.

title: Receipt of mysterious Xerox Missive from Austria (Osterreich)
kyle_arnold_account: Arnold analyzes Dick's interpretation. Envelope contained xeroxed book review about American capitalism collapse with underlined 'die words' (destruction, annihilation, decomposition). Dick feared it was KGB recruitment attempt or FBI loyalty test. He called FBI declaring himself 'a dangerous machine' and should be incarcerated. They ignored him.
sutin_account: Mentioned in Arnold as part of Dick's paranoid infrastructure during 2-3-74. Demonstrates how real ambiguous stimulus (book review) was woven into fear structure.
religious_context: Part of apocalyptic framework: unseen forces testing/persecuting Dick. Cosmic significance attributed to mundane item.
location: Postmark: Austria (Osterreich); received at Dick's apartment
people_involved: Philip K. Dick, FBI, KGB (in Dick's imagination), Tessa B. Dick (who received and read it)
significance: Shows intersection of paranoia and revelation. Dick's logic: if persecuted, then important; if important, then divine mission justified. Arnold argues this is chronic paranoia pattern, not new pathology.

title: Shoulder injury from seashell throw; diagnosis of son's hernia through mystical insight
kyle_arnold_account: Arnold notes Dick injured shoulder during argument with Tessa. While recovering from surgery, Dick heard son Christopher's babbling as Aramaic: 'Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani' (Christ's crucifixion cry). Arnold notes: 'Although his intuition of his son's medical condition was not as miraculous as he claimed...it was accurate and contributed to his son's treatment.'
sutin_account: Arnold documents Dick 'awoke to the sound of his son babbling, and heard it as a series of pleas spoken in Aramaic.' Pink light warned Dick that Christopher had 'a dire medical condition.' The revelation appeared valid: Christopher did have a treatable hernia.
religious_context: Dick uses this as proof of VALIS's existence and benevolence. 'Pink light' warning saved son's life. Interpreted as evidence of divine intervention. For Dick, this became central to justifying 2-3-74 as authentic mystical experience rather than delusion.
location: Dick family apartment; hospital (for Dick's shoulder surgery and Christopher's treatment)
people_involved: Philip K. Dick, Christopher (infant son), Tessa B. Dick
significance: Crucial convergence point: real medical benefit emerging from mystical experience. Arnold emphasizes Dick's and Tessa's previous suspicions about Christopher's health; Dick's 'intuition' may have simply been attentive parenting. But the outcome was genuinely beneficial.

title: Decline and fading of primary visionary experiences
kyle_arnold_account: Arnold notes: 'After August of 1974, Dick's religious experiences decreased in frequency and intensity.' No longer dominated entire subjective experience. However, 'Dick's mind remained intellectually fixed on 2-3-74 throughout the rest of his life.'
sutin_account: The visions that had sustained and structured Dick's consciousness since February began to fade. The divine spirit he felt inhabit him withdrew.
religious_context: End of primary 2-3-74 period. Beginning of what Arnold calls 'psychospiritual contraction'—the painful withdrawal following expansion.
people_involved: Philip K. Dick, Tessa B. Dick
significance: Marks transition from active mystical experience to obsessive intellectual engagement with experience. Leads to creation of the Exegesis and VALIS trilogy. Arnold: 'The door hit him on the way out, so to speak.'

title: IRS persecution anxiety, financial crisis, psychiatric hospitalization
kyle_arnold_account: Arnold emphasizes these contextual factors: 'By February of 1974, Dick was so incapacitated by the vicious cycle of his anxieties that he could not bring himself to go to the bank to deposit his royalty checks, and had to rely on Tessa to do so.' IRS had seized his car in 1971. Dick feared asset seizure again. Spent time at X-Kalay drug rehabilitation facility in Vancouver (1972-1973). Had psychiatric hospitalizations in 1973.
sutin_account: Phil 'didn't socialize much.' 'Deep down Phil was scared silly.' He believed he was 'programmed to die in 3-74' and feared fifteen years in prison for 'civil disobedience' during Vietnam War tax protest. 'The April 1974 filing was coming up. Phil was broke.'
religious_context: Apocalyptic framework: Dick felt doomed by external forces (government, CIA, KGB). 2-3-74 reframes this doom as divine revelation and testing rather than mere persecution.
location: Fullerton, California; Vancouver X-Kalay (1972-1973); psychiatric hospitals
people_involved: Philip K. Dick, Tessa B. Dick, IRS, psychiatrists, drug counselors
significance: Arnold argues these mundane stressors explain 2-3-74's initiation without requiring supernatural causation. Sutin emphasizes Dick's genuine terror. Both agree: psychological/financial/medical vulnerability set stage.

title: Baptism experience: vision of red devil leaving baptistry
kyle_arnold_account: Not specifically covered by Arnold; contextual religious experience.
sutin_account: Phil, Anne, and kids baptized together January 1964. 'As we drove home Phil told me cheerfully, "At the moment of my baptism I saw, slinking out of the baptistry, his tail between his legs, a small red devil, the classic type, with horns and a spiked tail."'
religious_context: Shows Dick's lifelong pattern of interpolating visions into religious ritual. The devil represents the false authority/demiurge later developed into Black Iron Prison theology.
people_involved: Philip K. Dick, Anne Rubinstein Dick, children, clergy
significance: Early instance of Dick's mystical/visionary tendency during religious ceremony. Precursor to 2-3-74's more elaborate visionary interpolations.

title: Amphetamine abuse escalation and paranoid ideation deepening
kyle_arnold_account: Arnold documents: Dick's paranoia intensified throughout 1960s-early 1970s. By 1971, 'zenith of Dick's amphetamine-fueled paranoia.' Feared CIA tapping his phone, FBI monitoring, mother/stepfather stealing house. Hired two bodyguards. Amphetamine use was chronic and escalating.
sutin_account: Phil was 'always less gregarious when married.' His relationships with women created stress. He moved repeatedly. Drug use provided creative fuel but also psychological destabilization.
religious_context: Amphetamine paranoia creates apocalyptic/conspiratorial mindset that later finds religious expression in 2-3-74's Black Iron Prison cosmology.
location: California residences (Bay Area and Marin County)
people_involved: Philip K. Dick, various wives (Anne, Nancy, Tessa), psychiatrists, various suspected persecutors
significance: Arnold's central argument: 2-3-74's paranoid features are not 'acute onset' but continuation of chronic baseline paranoia developed over years of amphetamine abuse. 'By 1974, paranoia was business as usual for Dick.'

title: Suicide attempt: digitalis overdose, wrist-cutting, car exhaust
kyle_arnold_account: Arnold documents: Tessa walked out during argument, taking son and half furniture. That night Dick 'swallowed forty-nine tablets of his blood pressure medication digitalis.' Also ingested 'smaller overdoses of psychotropic medications, washing it all down with a half-bottle of wine.' Then 'slit his wrist, cutting deeply enough that his blood sprayed up onto his ceiling.' Finally went to garage to start car for carbon monoxide. 'However, all three methods miscarried: the car stalled, the blood coagulated, and Dick threw up the pills.'
sutin_account: Later fictionalized in VALIS. Dick claimed the attempt 'paradoxically saved his life' by uncovering potassium deficiency.
religious_context: The 'divine spirit left him,' leaving despair that prompted suicide attempt. Arnold: 'massive contraction' following 2-3-74 expansion. 'Consciousness is like a rubber band: the more you stretch it, the harder it snaps back' (Saniel Bonder).
location: Dick's apartment and garage, Fullerton, California
people_involved: Philip K. Dick, Tessa B. Dick (departed), Christopher (son)
significance: Shows aftermath trauma of 2-3-74's withdrawal. Arnold argues Dick's post-1974 life includes 'at least two suicide attempts, two psychiatric hospitalizations, self-defeating relationships, and bouts of severe depression.' Not evidence of metanoiac healing.

title: Exegesis obsession and fictionalization of 2-3-74
kyle_arnold_account: Arnold documents: Dick produced four novels about 2-3-74: VALIS, The Divine Invasion, Radio Free Albemuth, and uncompleted Transmigration of Timothy Archer. Created eight-thousand-page Exegesis journal (nearly eight years). Dick 'was obsessed, much as he had been with the phantom burglary.' He spun theories drawing from 'religious literature, philosophy, psychoanalysis, medicine, and science fiction.'
sutin_account: Phil 'never really doubted that the visions and auditions of February-March 1974 (2-3-74) and after had fundamentally changed his life.' Exegesis represents first comprehensive study of VALIS material. VALIS (published 1981) 'was completed in November of 1978.' The Exegesis became 'primary inspiration' for published novels.
religious_context: Dick attempts to construct grand theological system explaining 2-3-74 through Gnostic, Neoplatonic, and Christian frameworks. The Exegesis documents his struggle to determine if revelation was authentic or delusional.
people_involved: Philip K. Dick, Tessa B. Dick, various literary collaborators and biographers
significance: 2-3-74 becomes Dick's life work. Arnold: 'self-doubt was more fundamental than any deliberate technique. Entries in the Exegesis indicate, time and again, that even when not writing for an audience Dick continued to second-guess his experiences.' Paradox: Dick both evangelizes 2-3-74 as proof of divine existence and doubts his own sanity.

title: Reflection: 'The Restorer of What Was Lost'—letter to Claudia Bush
kyle_arnold_account: Arnold cites this as key retrospective document. Dick attempts one-year retrospective assessment of experiences, suggesting some consolidation and processing had occurred.
sutin_account: On March 21, 1975, 'one year later, Phil wrote as concise and radiant a summary of the visions as he ever achieved: I speak of The Restorer of What Was Lost The Mender of What Was Broken.' This marks transition from active visionary experience to interpretive/theological engagement.
religious_context: Dick attempts to integrate 2-3-74 into coherent spiritual narrative. The 'Restorer' becomes central organizing metaphor for Exegesis theology.
significance: Shows Dick's effort to create meaning from chaotic visionary experiences. Arnold notes this is characteristic of his psychology: need to narrativize and theorize experience continuously.
